Description: Svelte 5 $state rune replaces let declarations for reactive state — explicit and compiler-optimised
Do: Declare mutable reactive state with $state()
Don't: Use plain let for state that needs to be reactive in Svelte 5
Code Bad: let count = 0 // not reactive in Svelte 5

Description: $derived() memoises expressions that depend on reactive state — replaces $: reactive statements
Do: Derive values with $derived() instead of $: labels
Don't: Use $: for derived values in Svelte 5

Description: $effect() runs after DOM updates when its reactive dependencies change — replaces onMount + reactive statements for side-effects
Do: Use $effect() for DOM interactions and subscriptions
Don't: Use $: blocks for side-effects that need cleanup in Svelte 5

Description: Return a cleanup function from $effect to cancel subscriptions and timers when the component is destroyed or deps change
Do: Always return cleanup logic from $effect
Don't: Leave subscriptions running after component teardown

Description: $props() rune replaces export let for component inputs — provides destructuring and default values in one line
Do: Use const { name = 'World' } = $props() for component props
Don't: Use export let for props in Svelte 5 components
Code Bad: export let label; export let disabled = false // Svelte 4 pattern

Description: $state.snapshot() creates a plain deep copy of reactive state — safe to pass to external APIs or serialize
Do: Use $state.snapshot(data) when passing state to non-reactive contexts
Don't: Pass reactive $state proxies directly to JSON.stringify / fetch

Guideline: Prefer snippets over slot fallback in Svelte 5
Description: Svelte 5 snippets ({#snippet}) replace slots — type-safe and composable component content blocks
Do: Use {#snippet} and {@render} for component content areas
Don't: Use legacy <slot> syntax in new Svelte 5 components

Guideline: Pass snippets as props for reuse
Description: Snippets can be passed as typed props enabling render-prop-style composition without external libs
Do: Accept Snippet<[]> typed props and render with @render
Don't: Duplicate template markup across components

Description: Each component should do one thing — split display logic from data-fetching and from layout
Do: Create focused leaf components for display
Don't: Build large page-level components with mixed concerns

Guideline: Use writable stores for shared mutable state
Description: Svelte writable stores are reactive across the whole app — subscribe with $ prefix in templates
Do: Create writable stores for cross-component state
Don't: Use module-level variables for shared state
Code Bad: export let count = 0 // not reactive across components

Guideline: Use derived stores for computed global state
Description: derived() creates a read-only store computed from other stores — avoids duplicating derivation logic
Do: Use derived() for computed global values
Don't: Subscribe to multiple stores and compute in each component
Code Good: const total = derived(cart n => n.reduce((s i) => s + i.price 0))
Code Bad: // repeating reduce logic in every component

Guideline: Unsubscribe from stores to prevent leaks
Description: Manual store.subscribe() calls must be unsubscribed in onDestroy — or use the $ auto-subscription shorthand
Do: Use $store syntax in templates for auto-subscribe/unsubscribe
Don't: Manually subscribe without cleanup
Code Bad: const unsub = count.subscribe(v => {}); // must call unsub() in onDestroy

Description: SvelteKit derives routes from the src/routes/ directory — +page.svelte and +layout.svelte are the conventions
Do: Follow +page.svelte / +layout.svelte / +error.svelte naming
Don't: Create custom router logic or dynamic component switching
Code Bad: src/routes/BlogPage.svelte // not picked up by router

Description: Shared navigation and shell UI belongs in +layout.svelte — child routes inherit it automatically
Do: Wrap shared chrome in +layout.svelte
Don't: Repeat <Nav> and <Footer> in every +page.svelte

Guideline: Use route groups for layout variants
Description: Wrap routes in (group)/ directories to share a layout without affecting the URL path
Do: Use (auth)/ and (public)/ route groups for layout variants
Don't: Create duplicate layout files or use conditional rendering

Description: Server-side load functions run on the server — safe for DB queries and secret env vars
Do: Fetch data in load() inside +page.server.ts
Don't: Call fetch with secret keys from client-side onMount
Code Good: export const load = async () => ({ posts: await db.getPosts() })

Guideline: Return typed data from load with satisfies
Description: Use satisfies PageServerLoad to get inferred page data types without losing specificity
Do: Type load return with satisfies or PageServerLoad generic
Don't: Return untyped objects from load and cast in the component
Code Good: export const load = (async () => ({ user })) satisfies PageServerLoad
Code Bad: export function load() { return { user } } // no types

Description: +page.server.ts actions handle form submissions server-side — progressive enhancement works without JS
Do: Use actions for form mutations (create/update/delete)
Don't: Use API routes for every form submission
Code Good: export const actions = { create: async ({ request }) => { ... } }
Code Bad: fetch('/api/create' { method: 'POST' body }) // skips SvelteKit actions

Guideline: Preload routes on hover with data-sveltekit-preload-data
Description: SvelteKit can prefetch a route's load data on hover — near-instant navigation for users
Do: Add data-sveltekit-preload-data="hover" to <a> or layout
Don't: Skip preloading and let users wait for data on click

Guideline: Lazy-load heavy components with dynamic import
Description: import() splits heavy components into separate JS chunks — reduces initial page weight
Do: Use dynamic imports for modals and below-the-fold components
Don't: Import all components statically at the top of the script

Description: Enhanced-img generates modern formats (avif/webp) and correct srcset at build time — no manual work
Do: Use <enhanced:img> for all content images
Don't: Use raw with unoptimised large files

Description: Svelte's built-in transition directive applies enter/leave animations declaratively — no imperative JS needed
Do: Use transition:fade or transition:slide on conditional elements
Don't: Use CSS classes toggled with JS for show/hide animations

Guideline: Use animate: for keyed list reordering
Description: animate:flip handles list item reorder animations automatically when using keyed each blocks
Do: Add animate:flip to elements in keyed {#each} blocks
Don't: Animate list reorders with manual GSAP/JS position tracking
Code Bad: // manually calculating element positions for animation

Description: Semantic elements convey meaning to assistive technologies — do not replace them with div/span clones
Do: Use <button> <nav> <main> <article> <header> etc
Don't: Use <div> with on:click or role="button" for interactive elements

Guideline: Bind ARIA state to reactive variables
Description: ARIA attributes reflecting component state must update reactively — static aria values mislead screen readers
Do: Use aria-expanded={isOpen} and aria-disabled={disabled}
Don't: Hardcode aria attribute values
